Tsinghua University: Densing Law of LLMs (Nature Machine Intelligence cover article). Maximum capability density of open-source LLMs roughly doubles every 3.5 months; a model with half the parameters can match the state of the art about every 3.5 months. Dataset: 51 open models, Feb 2023 to Apr 2025. Assumes models trained equally well have the same density; describes the best open models, not typical ones.

description: BigGo Finance report on a Counterpoint Research forecast (Kang Kyung-soo, iForum 2026, 22 Oct 2026): new memory output from SK Hynix and Micron from 2027, Samsung and CXMT expansions ramp in 2028; headline cites prices reversing to a 20-30% decline by 2028. Same article: TrendForce expects consumer memory prices to keep rising next year; Q3 2026 DRAM contract prices +13-18% quarter on quarter.
TweakTown headline: 'Memory shortages will get only worse in 2027 and 2028, warns Samsung'. Article could not be retrieved; headline only, treat as unverified.
God Is A Geek: RTX 6090 rumoured for H1 2027 (Moore's Law Is Dead, 14 Sep 2026); leakers dispute it and suggest 2028; up to 32 GB GDDR7 in unattributed leaks. NVIDIA has announced nothing.
TechCrunch, citing Appfigures: new app releases Q1 2026 versus Q1 2025 +60% worldwide (+80% on iOS); April 2026 to date +104% (+89% iOS). AI coding tools are the suspected cause, not measured.

9to5Mac, citing The Information and Sensor Tower: new App Store apps grew 30% to nearly 600,000 in 2025 versus 2024; the report suggests vibe-coding tools are the main contributors but cannot say how many apps were AI-built.

IDC and Omdia Q3 2026 PC shipments, as reported by Digital Today (Korea) and Windows Latest: IDC -20.1% to 62.7M units (from 78.5M); Omdia -21.2% to 58.1M (laptops, desktops, workstations). Both attribute the fall to the AI-driven memory squeeze. Neither article gives an AI-PC share.

Canalys, as reported by Vivre and Computer Weekly: AI-capable PCs were 14% of global shipments in Q2 2024 (8.8M units) and 20% in Q3 2024 (13.3M units). Definition: a desktop or notebook with a chipset or block for dedicated AI workloads, such as a neural processing unit (NPU).

Tom's Hardware, 'What is an AI PC': Microsoft Copilot+ PC requires an NPU of at least 40 TOPS, 16 GB RAM and 256 GB storage; Intel defines an AI PC as having a CPU, GPU and NPU with AI acceleration. The article does not say whether these PCs can run large language models locally.

GitHub topic pages, public repositories matching the topic: 'ollama' 5,794 and 'local-llm' 9,477 (page counts, 25 Oct 2026). Counts include libraries, tools and forks, not only end-user apps; overlap between topics not removed.
